controls.name: broken
controls.description: verdict reported correctly but the transcoded UTF-16LE units are corrupted, so the pristine payload never matches the in-eval trusted reference; scored zero on every split

controls.name: naive
controls.description: hand-written scalar strict UTF-8 validator/transcoder, one code point at a time, byte-identical output but ~1.7x slower than the SIMD kernels

controls.name: shortcut
controls.description: train-overfit that keys on the TRAIN-only corpus header marker: runs the genuine single-pass fast path (correct+faster than baseline) where the marker is present, and emits corrupted output on the held-out validation corpus it never memorized, so it beats baseline on train (1.148 > 1.0) and inverts to zero on validation, which the trusted split mechanism catches

perturbation.name: streamlined-validate-then-fast-convert
perturbation.description: genuine observation-preserving work reduction: the baseline driver validates, then runs a utf16-length pre-scan, then a fully re-validating conversion pass (validate + length + slow validating convert); the improved driver validates once and then uses the non-validating fast conversion path (convert_valid), dropping the redundant length pre-scan and the re-validation. Byte-identical verdict + transcoded bytes to the baseline on every corpus/iteration (the trusted parent re-checks the go-nonce-bound 8-lane digest against the pristine reference each timed iteration); ~14.7% faster (12.9 sigma over the A-A noise), and holds on both train and validation.

rss.note: whole-tree kernel cgroup2 memory.peak of a fresh per-launch leaf (worker.py python startup then the trusted runner + dlopened simdutf library + corpus/scratch/out buffers). Observed baseline peaks ~5.5-7.5 MiB (python-startup dominated, noisy under page-cache reclaim); frozen at 9216 KiB so the improved control and measurement noise clear the gate while a gross whole-tree regression fails. Both ordering passes had peak_rss=true on baseline/naive/improved across both splits.

execBoundary.model: The scored measurement loop AND the receipt handshake run in the trusted parent (eval.py) and a trusted runner (hone/runner.cpp) that links NO candidate code. The runner authenticates the parent's control channel and echoes READY, then dlopens the candidate library (memfd-loaded to dodge noexec) and resolves its C ABI; the per-leg perturbation seed and receipt fold nonce arrive over the control pipe only after the library is mapped (the GO line, clock-start). A candidate constructor / .init_array therefore runs AFTER auth and BEFORE the go-time fold nonce exists, so it cannot precompute a matching digest.
execBoundary.demonstration: A stub candidate whose constructor forged LOADED + a fake RESULT and _exit(0) (discovering the response fd) produced a digest that did NOT match the pristine reference and returned in ~0.04ms; the trusted parent rejected it on both the digest-mismatch check and the implausible-speedup floor (candidate wall < reference/8). Demonstrated pre-freeze against the trusted runner, then deleted.

normalization.status: 2x-consecutive bench-locked ordering (min-of-N estimator for ~0.6s legs under persistent Docker-VM background contention, 8-lane output fold, whole-tree cgroup memory.peak, fresh IPC ns). qBase/sigma from the 6 baseline A-A stability aggregates across both passes; final frozen like-for-like GCE re-calibration still required.
